verses.text: Early in the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this message came from the LORD:

"This is what the LORD says: 'Stand in the courtyard of the LORD's temple and speak to the people of all the towns of Judah who come to worship in the LORD's temple. Tell them everything I command you. Do not leave out a single word.
Maybe they will listen, and each one will turn from their evil ways. Then I may change my mind about the disaster I plan to bring on them because of the evil they have done.'
Tell them, 'This is what the LORD says: If you will not listen to me and follow my law, which I have set before you,
and if you will not listen to the words of my servants the prophets, whom I have sent to you again and again, though you have not listened,
then I will make this temple like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse among all the nations of the earth.'"
The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speak these words in the LORD's temple.
As soon as Jeremiah finished telling all the people everything the LORD had commanded him to say, the priests, the prophets, and all the people grabbed him and said, "You must die!
Why do you prophesy in the LORD's name that this temple will be like Shiloh and this city will be a ruin with no one living in it?" And all the people crowded around Jeremiah in the LORD's temple.
When the officials of Judah heard about this, they went up from the king's palace to the LORD's temple and sat down at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD's temple.
Then the priests and the prophets said to the officials and to all the people, "This man deserves to die, because he has prophesied against this city. You have heard it with your own ears."
Then Jeremiah said to all the officials and all the people, "The LORD sent me to prophesy against this temple and this city all the words you have heard.
So now change your ways and your actions, and obey the LORD your God. Then the LORD will change his mind about the disaster he has announced against you.
As for me, I am in your hands. Do with me whatever you think is good and right.

But know this for certain: if you put me to death, you will bring the guilt of innocent blood on yourselves, on this city, and on the people who live here. For it is true that the LORD sent me to you to speak all these words for you to hear."
Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, "This man does not deserve to die. He has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God."
Some of the elders of the land stood up and said to the whole assembly of people,

"Micah from Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. He told all the people of Judah, 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: Zion will be plowed like a field. Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble, and the temple hill will become a hill covered with forest.'

Did Hezekiah king of Judah or anyone in Judah put him to death? Didn't Hezekiah fear the LORD and ask for the LORD's favor? And didn't the LORD change his mind about the disaster he had announced against them? We are about to bring terrible harm on ourselves!"
There was another man who prophesied in the LORD's name, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath Jearim. He prophesied against this city and this land the same things Jeremiah did.
When King Jehoiakim, all his soldiers, and all the officials heard what he said, the king tried to have him killed. But Uriah heard about it and was afraid, so he ran away to Egypt.
Then King Jehoiakim sent Elnathan son of Achbor and some other men to Egypt.
They brought Uriah back from Egypt to King Jehoiakim, who had him killed with a sword. His body was thrown into the burial place of the common people.
But Ahikam son of Shaphan supported Jeremiah, so he was not handed over to the people to be put to death.
